This page covers four regression tests:

- `npsigtest` for nonparametric regression significance testing,
- `npcmstest` for consistent model specification testing,
- `npindextest` for a single-index restriction,
- `nppltest` for a partially linear conditional mean.

Minimal downloadable scripts for the two established routes are:

- [np_significance_quickstart.R](www/np_npRmpi/np_significance_quickstart.R)
- [np_specification_quickstart.R](www/np_npRmpi/np_specification_quickstart.R)

`npsigtest()` chooses pivotal statistics for continuous predictors and unstandardized
statistics for categorical predictors by default; an explicit `pivot` choice
still overrides that automatic policy.

## Significance testing: `npsigtest`

For a fitted regression $g(x)=E(Y\mid X=x)$, `npsigtest()` tests whether a
selected predictor contributes to $g(x)$.

```r
## Fit a local-linear regression before calling the nonparametric significance test
library(np)
data(cps71, package = "np")

fit <- npreg(logwage ~ age,
  regtype = "ll",
  bwmethod = "cv.aic",
  gradients = TRUE,
  data = cps71)

npsigtest(fit)
```

The test retains the nonparametric regression specification rather than
replacing it with a linear model.

## Model specification testing: `npcmstest`

`npcmstest()` tests a parametric conditional-mean specification against a
consistent nonparametric alternative.

The `wage1` example starts with a simple linear specification and then asks
whether that specification is too restrictive.

```r
## Compare a simple linear model to a nonparametric alternative
library(np)
data(wage1, package = "np")

model_ols <- lm(lwage ~ female + married + educ + exper + tenure,
  x = TRUE,
  y = TRUE,
  data = wage1)

X <- data.frame(female = wage1$female,
  married = wage1$married,
  educ = wage1$educ,
  exper = wage1$exper,
  tenure = wage1$tenure)

test_out <- npcmstest(model = model_ols,
  xdat = X,
  ydat = wage1$lwage)

summary(test_out)
```

## Single-index specification: `npindextest`

For a continuous response, `npindextest()` asks whether
$E(Y\mid X)=g(X^\mathsf{T}\beta)$. For a binary response it tests the analogous
restriction on the success probability. Every bootstrap draw refits the index
direction and link bandwidth.

The short script below fits correctly specified and off-index alternatives for
both Ichimura and Klein--Spady models. With seed 42, the default test retains
both nulls and rejects both alternatives at 5%.

## Partial-linearity specification: `nppltest`

`nppltest()` asks whether
$E(Y\mid X,Z)=X^\mathsf{T}\beta+g(Z)$ rather than an unrestricted conditional
mean. The default uses 2,048 shifted Sobol projection directions;
`integration = "exact"` requests analytical angular integration.

The script below retains a partially linear null and rejects an alternative
with curvature in a regressor assigned to the linear component.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

All ten public specification, significance, and distribution tests now default
to 399 bootstrap draws. Their reported p-values count draws at least as extreme
as the observed statistic, including ties, and summaries report elapsed time.

## Practical warning

These tests can be computationally demanding because they may involve both bandwidth selection and bootstrap procedures.

Practical advice:

- begin with a small problem when exploring a specification,
- budget separately for estimation and testing,
- preserve the default search tolerances unless a deliberate exploratory run requires otherwise.

## When should I use these?

| Question | Function |
|---|---|
| Is a regressor significant in a nonparametric regression setting? | `npsigtest` |
| Does a parametric regression model look misspecified against a nonparametric alternative? | `npcmstest` |
| Does a fitted link depend on the covariates through one linear index? | `npindextest` |
| Is the conditional mean partially linear in the designated regressors? | `nppltest` |
